title: Medicare Program; Contract Year 2028 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, and Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly
summary: This proposed rule would revise the Medicare Advantage (Part C), Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit (Part D), and Programs of All- Inclusive Care for the Elderly regulations to implement changes related to marketing and communications, drug coverage, enrollment processes, special needs plans, and other programmatic areas. Additionally, it would establish and implement a mandatory Medicare Advantage (MA) CMS Innovation Center model.

title: Renaming Narcotic Treatment Program (NTP) to Opioid Treatment Program (OTP) in DEA Regulations
summary: This final rule updates Drug Enforcement Administration regulations to change the name of Narcotic Treatment Programs to Opioid Treatment Programs. This action is a nomenclature change and makes no substantive changes to the definition of a narcotic drug in the Controlled Substances Act or the definition of a narcotic treatment program in the implementing regulations.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. Airplanes
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-11- 08, which applied to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-6, PC-6-H1, PC-6-H2, PC-6/350, PC-6/350-H1, PC-6/350-H2, PC-6/A, PC-6/A- H1, PC-6/A-H2, PC-6/B-H2, PC-6/B1-H2, PC-6/B2-H2, PC-6/B2-H4, PC-6/C- H2, and PC-6/C1-H2 airplanes. AD 2021-11-08 required revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) to incorporate new airworthiness limitations and adding an additional eddy current inspection of the fuselage wing fittings and wing-to-fuselage fittings if the last inspection was performed using an earlier version of the required material. Since the FAA issued AD 2021- 11-08, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing AMM or ICA for these airplanes. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Peppered Shiner
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the peppered shiner (Miniellus perpallidus), a fish species from southeast Oklahoma and southern Arkansas, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the peppered shiner. After a review of the best available scientific and commercial information, we find that listing the species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the peppered shiner as an endangered species under the Act. If finalized as proposed, this rule would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the Rio Grande Shiner
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Rio Grande shiner (Notropis jemezanus), a fish species from the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico, Texas, and Mexico, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Rio Grande shiner. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500- 1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of multiple in-service failures of pressure regulating shutoff valves (PRSOVs). This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to incorporate procedures for reducing the thrust lever or shutting down the engine when the BLEED LEAK caution message is persistent, prohibits operation in known or forecasted icing conditions under certain minimum equipment list (MEL) provisions where the only operative PRSOV is an affected part, and requires replacement of affected PRSOVs with improved PRSOVs. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Canton, TX
summary: This action proposes to establish Class E airspace at Mother Frances-Canton Heliport, Canton, TX. The FAA is proposing this action to support new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 757-200 and -300 series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of missing and/or incorrectly installed lockwire on backshells found during engineering validation tests in the wing leading edge and engine struts for high intensity radiated field (HIRF)/lightning protection features. This proposed AD would require inspection of the backshells at the left- and right-wing leading edge and nacelle strut for missing and incorrectly installed lockwire and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-04, which applies to all Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-04 requires a one-time detailed inspection of the engine nacelle anti-icing (NAI) forward bulkhead locating holes for elongation and loose fasteners and applicable corrective actions and prohibits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-04, it has been determined that affected parts must accumulate at least 2,000 flight cycles (FC) since installation prior to the inspection to ensure that the inspection will detect discrepancies. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-19-04 and would amend the compliance time for the inspection. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Atka Mackerel in the Bering Sea Subarea and Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
summary: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Atka mackerel in the Bering Sea subarea and Eastern Aleutian District (BS/EAI) of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI) by vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery. This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Atka mackerel in the BS/EAI allocated to vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery.

title: Control of Communicable Diseases; Foreign Quarantine
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), is extending the expiration date of the interim final rule published on May 27, 2026. This interim final rule removes an exemption for lawful permanent residents from application of regulations implementing section 362 of the Public Health Service (PHS) Act, which authorizes the Secretary, acting through the CDC Director or other delegate, to suspend the introduction of persons from designated countries or places, if required, in the interest of public health.

title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Pacific Ocean Perch in the Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
summary: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Pacific ocean perch in the Eastern Aleutian district (EAI) of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI) by vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery. This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Pacific ocean perch in the EAI allocated to vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery.

title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.

title: Corporate Credit Unions
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.

title: Supervisory Committee Audits And Verifications
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing supervisory committee audits to eliminate unnecessary, redundant, and overly prescriptive provisions. The final rule is necessary to reduce regulatory burden, increase operational flexibility for federally insured credit unions (FICUs), and streamline the rules by removing requirements that are outdated or duplicative of other authorities. The intended effect of the final rule is to simplify compliance for FICUs without compromising the integrity of the audit process.

title: Additions to the Entity List
summary: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 7 entities to the Entity List, under the destinations of Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States.

title: Petition for Rulemaking To Consider Amendments to Regulations Governing Interim Use of Rights-of-Way as Trails
summary: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

title: VIAVI Solutions; Filing of Color Additive Petition
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is announcing that we have filed a color additive petition, submitted by VIAVI Solutions, proposing that the color additive regulations be amended to provide for the safe use of magnesium fluoride-aluminum flake for use in nail polish at a maximum level of 16 percent of the final product.

title: Safety Zone; Brownsville Ship Channel, Brownsville, TX
summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Brownsville Ship Channel. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with an over-sized dead ship tow transiting the area. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Corpus Christi, or their designated representative.

title: Auction of Flexible-Use Licenses in the Upper C-Band for Next-Generation Wireless Services; Notice and Filing Requirements, Minimum Opening Bids, Upfront Payments, and Other Procedures for Auction 115; Bidding Scheduled To Begin April 27, 2027
summary: This document summarizes the procedures, deadlines, upfront payment, and minimum opening bid amounts adopted in the Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice for the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) upcoming auction of 3,248 new flexible-use licenses in the 3.98-4.14 GHz portion of the Upper C-band. The Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice summarized here provides details regarding the procedures, terms, conditions, dates, and deadlines governing participation in Auction 115 bidding, as well as an overview of the post-auction application and payment processes.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 707 airplanes; Model 720 and 720B series airplanes; Model 727C, 727-100, -100C, -200, and -200F series airplanes; and Model 747-100, -100B, -100B SUD, -200B, -200C, -200F, - 300, 747SR, and 747SP series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports that using some adaptors while performing tests of the cabin altitude warning switch (CAWS) could lead to incorrect failures. This proposed AD would require repetitive operational tests or replacements of the CAWS and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK
summary: This action establishes Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface at Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK. This action supports the safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at the airport.

title: National Adoption Month, 2026
Protecting the Executive's Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting
Notification of Inflation Adjustments for Civil Money Penalties
summary: This document announces the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's (OCC) maximum civil money penalties for 2026 as adjusted for inflation. The inflation adjustments are required to implement the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, as amended by the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015.

title: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf-Documents Incorporated by Reference
summary: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), through Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), is incorporating by reference a collection of production measurement industry standards and safety industry standards into its regulations governing oil, gas, and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS). Incorporation of these documents by reference will provide industry with up-to-date, minimum requirements for measuring oil and gas production volumes and enhancing safety. Compliance with these standards will reduce uncertainty in the measurement of oil and gas production and update the minimum standards in the safety regulations.

title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2018-26-01 for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. AD 2018- 26-01 required initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. Since the FAA issued AD 2018-26-01, CFM issued updated service material providing improvements to the ultrasonic inspection procedures and expanding the inspection area. This AD requires initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Personnel Appeals Board; Procedural Rules
summary: The Government Accountability Office Personnel Appeals Board (PAB or Board) is amending several significant changes to its existing regulations to streamline and modernize case processing before the Board. The General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980 provides authority to make these changes.

title: Establishment of Class E Airspace Over Hardy, VA
summary: This action establishes new Class E airspace over Hardy, VA. This airspace is necessary to support Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations, utilizing new Special Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) serving Carilion Westlake Center Heliport.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model H160-B helicopters. This AD was prompted by a determination that a gap without fire-resistant sealant (sealant) may be present in the cargo bay near the fuel segregation box. This AD requires inspecting for any missing sealant and, depending on findings, corrective action. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-08-51, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-3 helicopters. AD 2026-08-51 requires inspecting the rotor hub-shaft for cracks, replacing any rotor hub- shaft that has any crack, and reporting information after accomplishment of the replacement. AD 2026-08-51 also prohibits installing any affected rotor hub-shaft on any helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-08-51, it was determined that additional repetitive inspections (including eddy current inspections) are necessary, and that revising the compliance time to account for hoist operations is necessary. This proposed AD would retain the actions of AD 2026-08-51 and would require additional repetitive inspections. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 429 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of premature wear-out of certain spherical bearings due to a quality escape of the spherical bearing monoballs not receiving the required hard coating. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the tail rotor (TR) pitch link assemblies and their bearings for cracks, wear, and mechanical or corrosion damage and, depending on the results, replacing any affected TR pitch link assembly. This AD also allows an affected part to be installed in a helicopter if certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-08-06 which applied to certain Airbus Helicopters Model SA330J helicopters. AD 2025-08-06 required repetitively inspecting for a gap between the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling fan assembly rotor blade and the upper section of the guide vane bearing housing, replacing the MGB fan rotor bearings with serviceable bearings if necessary, and at a later compliance time replacing the MGB fan rotor bearing assembly with an improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, which constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections. Since AD 2025-08-06 was issued, the FAA determined that the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly should be extended. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-08-06 and increases the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly. This AD also prohibits installing any MGB fan rotor bearings and any MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-10-10, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N, SA 365 N1, AS 365 N2, and AS 365 N3 helicopters. AD 2024-10-10 requires a one-time inspection for proper positioning of the tail rotor (TR) actuator harness and cable tie installation and, depending on the results, corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-10-10, the manufacturer developed a modification to reroute the yaw harness that would apply to certain model helicopters. This proposed AD would retain some of the actions of AD 2024-10-10 and would also require, for certain model helicopters, modifying the helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Denial of Rehearing Requests by Operation of Law Under the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure
summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) is revising its regulations addressing the circumstances under which a request for rehearing is denied absent Commission action within a particular time frame. Currently, the Commission's regulations provide that unless the Commission acts upon a request for rehearing within 30 days after the request is filed, the request is denied. As revised in this final rule, the regulation will apply only to matters subject to the rehearing and judicial review provisions in the Federal Power Act (FPA) and Natural Gas Act (NGA).

title: Streamlining the Application Process for Grants for Adaptive Sports Programs for Disabled Veterans and Disabled Members of the Armed Forces
summary: This proposed rule would amend the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations that govern grants for adaptive sports programs for disabled veterans and disabled members of the armed forces to allow for a more efficient review and selection of applicants for the grant. This rule would ensure that the grant aligns with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards by requiring applicants to submit an application within the VA established deadline for submission; requiring that all adaptive sports grants be openly competed; and adding a new section on appropriate actions VA may take to enforce this part. The changes proposed by this rulemaking will improve program administration without negatively impacting the veteran athletes supported by these grants.

title: IFR Altitudes; Miscellaneous Amendments
summary: This amendment adopts miscellaneous amendments to the required IFR (instrument flight rules) altitudes and changeover points for certain Federal airways, jet routes, or direct routes for which a minimum or maximum en-route authorized IFR altitude is prescribed. This regulatory action is needed because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace under instrument conditions in the affected areas.

title: International Proof of Delivery Service
summary: The Postal Service is revising Mailing Standards of the United States Postal Service, International Mail Manual (IMM[supreg]), to reflect changes to product features for Priority Mail International[supreg] (PMI) and to introduce International Proof of Delivery as a new international extra service that will be available for PMI mailpieces to select destinations.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-21- 08, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, - 800, and -900ER series airplanes. AD 2026-21-08 required a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-21-08, the FAA has determined that the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of AD 2026-21-08 omits reference to a certain date. This AD retains all of the requirements of AD 2026- 21-08 and adds the omitted reference to the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of this AD. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights
summary: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.

title: Amendment of Class D Airspace and Class E Airspace Over Tri-Cities, TN
summary: This action amends Class D and Class E airspace over Tri- Cities, TN. Specifically, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class D and Class E surface area airspace by expanding the radius and lateral boundaries to the northeast and removing the Tri-Cities Class E surface area extension airspace to the northeast. Additionally, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class E transitional airspace beginning at 700 feet above the surface by expanding the lateral boundaries of the western portion of the airspace. Lastly, this action updates the airport name within the Class D and E legal descriptions and other outdated verbiage.

title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail
summary: Although the consolidated audit trail (the "CAT") continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the "SROs") to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the "CAT NMS Plan"). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.

title: Safety Zone; Pasquotank River Harbor, Elizabeth City, NC

title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42-500 and ATR72-212A airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of two in-service events during takeoff where an internal failure of the integrated air system control (IASC) software analog-to-digital converter generated erroneous pressure digital values, leading to uncommanded full-speed closure of the outflow valve and a high negative cabin altitude rate. This proposed AD would require installing improved IASC software. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected software under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42 and ATR72 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a review of mooring loads that revealed that winds within the currently defined wind profiles could lead to loads exceeding the certification limits on the nose landing gear (NLG) and main landing gear (MLG) while the airplane is moored. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate a revised maintenance procedure (MP) for mooring the airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Regulations Implementing the Privacy Act
summary: The Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission (OSHRC) is proposing revisions to its regulations implementing the Privacy Act of 1974. The proposed amendments to the Privacy Act regulations provide additional information on how to submit a Privacy Act request and revise the requirements for verifying a requester's identity.

title: Employee or Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
summary: This final rule rescinds the analysis for determining employee or independent contractor status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA or Act) set forth in the Department of Labor's (Department) regulations and replaces it with an analysis similar to what it published in a final rule promulgated in 2021, with several modifications and enhancements. In addition, this final rule amends provisions in the Department's regulations implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) to provide that employee or independent contractor status under those laws should be determined using the Department's FLSA analysis, as the FMLA and MSPA both incorporate the FLSA's scope of employment.

title: Miscellaneous Technical Amendments; Technical Amendment
summary: This technical amendment contains non-substantive corrections to address typographical errors, editorial errors, and outdated or incorrect references in various parts of FAA regulations.

title: Extension of Import Restrictions Imposed on Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Egypt
summary: This document amends U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations to reflect the extension of import restrictions on certain categories of archaeological and ethnological material from the Arab Republic of Egypt (Egypt), which were originally published in CBP Decision (CBP Dec.) 16-23, and subsequently extended and amended in CBP Dec. 21-17. The CBP regulations are being amended to reflect this further extension through November 30, 2031.

title: Cybersecurity Labeling for Internet of Things
summary: In this document, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (Bureau) of the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) seeks comment on recommendations for the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark (USCTM) program, a voluntary cybersecurity labeling program for wireless consumer Internet of Things (IoT) products. The Bureau seeks comment on the design and placement of the FCC IoT Label, display of product registry information, certification renewal, post-market surveillance, and procedures for complaints, noncompliant products, and program administrators that withdraw or whose authority is terminated. These actions would support the establishment and effective administration of the USCTM program and provide consumers with accessible cybersecurity information about certified IoT products.

title: Horse Protection Amendments; Extension of Postponement of Regulations
summary: On May 8, 2024, we published a final rule amending the horse protection regulations. The final rule was initially scheduled to go into effect on February 1, 2025, except for Sec. 11.19, which was effective on June 7, 2024. On January 28, 2025, we published a postponement of the effective date of the remaining provisions from February 1, 2025, to April 2, 2025. On March 21, 2025, we published a further delay of the effective date to February 1, 2026, and a request for comment on whether the length of the postponement should be extended. On January 28, 2026, based on developments following the issuance of the March 21, 2025, delay of effective date, we published a document further delaying the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2026. On November 13, 2026, we published a proposed rule to remove parts of the 2024 Horse Protection final rule that were vacated by Court order from the regulations, as well as proposing to withdraw the non-vacated parts and update the regulations. As a consequence, in this document, we are issuing an extension of the postponement of the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2027.

title: Amendment of Class D and E Airspace and Removal of Class E Airspace Over Lebanon, NH
summary: This action proposes to amend Class D and Class E airspace over Lebanon, NH. This action would increase the lateral dimensions of the Lebanon, NH, Class D airspace to appropriately contain Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations at the Lebanon Municipal Airport. This action would also update verbiage in the Class D airspace legal description to comply with current FAA guidance. This action would also update the geographic coordinates for the airport in both the Class D and Class E5 airspace legal descriptions. This action would also remove the exclusions for adjacent Class E5 airspace from the Lebanon, NH, Class E5 airspace legal description. This action would also remove the Lebanon, NH, Class E4 airspace, which is no longer necessary for IFR operations at the airport.

title: Connect America Fund; A National Broadband Plan for Our Future High-Cost Universal Support, Reforming the High-Cost Program for an All-IP Future, Safeguarding Universal Service Funding Through Effective Applicant Vetting
summary: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC or Commission) initiates a rulemaking to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, certain new funding awards of high-cost Universal Service Fund (USF) support.

title: Amendment of Class E Airspace; Del Rio, TX
summary: This action amends the Class E airspace at Del Rio, TX. This action is the result of a biennial review of the airspace associated with Laughlin Air Force Base (AFB), Del Rio, TX. This proposal also updates the name and geographic coordinates of Laughlin AFB to coincide with the FAA's aeronautical database. This action brings the airspace into compliance with FAA orders and supports instrument flight rule (IFR) procedures and operations.

title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Columbus, TX
summary: This action proposes to establish Class E airspace at Columbus Community Hospital Heliport, Columbus, TX. The FAA is proposing this action to support new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.

title: Safety Zone; Annual Fireworks Display Within the Sector Columbia River Captain of the Port Zone, Richland, WA
summary: The Coast Guard will enforce a safety zone for the City of Richland Lighted Boat Parade Fireworks on December 5, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waters during a fireworks display. Our regulation for the fireworks display within the Northwest Coast Guard District designates safety zones and identifies approximate dates for these events. Specific date and times are identified in this notice. These regulations prohibit persons and vessels from entering or remaining in the safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port Sector Columbia River or a Designated Representative.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a separated tail rotor blade (TRB) assembly due to a crack caused by intergranular corrosion. This AD requires repetitively inspecting a certain TRB assembly for cracks and, depending on the results, removing any cracked TRB assembly from service and replacing an affected part as terminating action for the repetitive inspections. This AD also prohibits installing a certain TRB assembly on any helicopter unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Reef Fish Fishery in the Gulf of America; 2026 Recreational Private Angling Component Closure for Red Snapper in Federal Waters off Texas
summary: NMFS closes the 2026 recreational fishing season for the red snapper private angling component in Federal waters of the Gulf of America (Gulf) off Texas. The recreational private angling component in Federal waters off Texas is closed on November 21, 2026, and this closure continues through the remainder of 2026. This red snapper closure is necessary to prevent the private angling component from exceeding the annual catch limit (ACL) in the Texas regional management area and to prevent overfishing of red snapper.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-13- 09, which applied to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS-365N2, AS 365 N3, EC 155B, EC155B1, SA-365N, and SA-365N1 helicopters. AD 2025-13-09 required inspecting the tightening torque, reporting the results of the inspections, and, depending on the results of the inspection, taking corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-13-09, the manufacturer determined that additional inspections of the main rotor (MR) servo-controls nut torque are required. This AD retains some of the actions of AD 2025-13-09 and requires additional inspections and, depending on the results of the inspection, corrective actions. This AD also requires reporting certain information to the manufacturer. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Air Plan Approval; Kentucky; Campbell-Clermont Area Maintenance Plan for the 2010 1-Hour SO2 NAAQS; Withdrawal of Direct Final Rule

title: Air Plan Approval; Arkansas; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference

The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by the State of Arkansas and approved by the EPA. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of crack damage at existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections. This AD requires doing an inspection for any existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Cotton Board Rules and Regulations: Adjusting Supplemental Assessment on Imports (2025 Amendments)
summary: The Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is amending the Cotton Board Rules and Regulations to decrease the value assigned to imported cotton for the purposes of calculating supplemental assessments collected for use by the Cotton Research and Promotion Program. This amendment is required each year to ensure that assessments collected on imported cotton, and the cotton content of imported products, will be the same as those paid on domestically produced cotton. In addition, AMS is updating the Import Assessment Table to account for changes since the last assessment adjustment in 2024.

title: Air Plan Approval; Oklahoma; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A330-841 and A330-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of cracks on the discharge outlet of certain engine fire extinguisher bottles. This AD requires modification of affected fire extinguisher bottles and prohibits the installation of affected parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, and -900 series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a review of the autothrottle (A/T) cruise thrust split monitor (MONFD) and the determination that there is a potential for latent loss of spoiler sensor position data or erroneous spoiler sensor position data. This AD requires repetitive aileron built-in test equipment (BITE) tests of the digital flight control system and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Special Local Regulations; Annual Marine Events on the Colorado River, Between Davis Dam (Bullhead City, Arizona) and Headgate Dam (Parker, Arizona), BlueWater Resort and Casino Thanksgiving Regatta, Colorado River, Parker, AZ

Our regulation for marine events within the Southwest Coast Guard District identifies the regulated area for this event in Parker, AZ. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Patrol Commander or any Official Patrol displaying a Coast Guard ensign.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries Off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; 2026 Tribal Fishery Allocations for Pacific Whiting; Reapportionment Between Tribal and Non-Tribal Sectors
summary: This document announces the reapportionment of 29,130 metric tons of Pacific whiting from the Tribal allocation to the non-Tribal commercial fishery sectors via automatic actions on September 14, and 23, and October 5, 2026. This reapportionment is to allow full utilization of the Pacific whiting resource.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.

title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
summary: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

title: Executive Compensation Disclosure Reform
summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is proposing amendments to its executive and director compensation disclosure rules to make the requirements more principles-based and to reduce compliance burdens for registrants, while maintaining the disclosure of material information to investors. The proposed amendments would focus the disclosures on the principal executive officer ("PEO") and principal financial officer ("PFO"), streamline the tabular disclosure requirements, and simplify and rationalize various other aspects of the compensation disclosure rules, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis ("CD&A"), pay ratio, pay- versus-performance, and perquisites disclosure requirements.

title: Mammoth Cave National Park; Bicycling and Horses
summary: The National Park Service (NPS) amends the special regulations for Mammoth Cave National Park to allow bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails throughout the park. This rule also will allow visitors to ride horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road.

title: Safety Zone; Hackensack River, Kearny and Secaucus, NJ
summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Hackensack River, in Kearny and Secaucus, NJ. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the demolition of the existing Portal Bridge. When subject to enforcement, entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector New York, or their designated representative.

title: Safety Zones; Annual Events Requiring Safety Zones in the Captain of the Port Lake Michigan Zone-Magnificent Mile Fireworks Display
summary: The Coast Guard will enforce a safety zone for the Magnificent Mile Fireworks Display on November 21, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during this fireworks display. Our regulation for marine events within the Great Lakes Coast Guard District identifies the safety zone for this event in Chicago, IL. During the enforcement period, entry into, transiting, or remaining within the safety zone is prohibited unless authorized by the Captain of the Port (COTP) Lake Michigan or his or her designated representative.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-12-08, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. AD 2026-12-08 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-12-08, a determination was made that new and more restrictive airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks are necessary. This proposed AD would require incorporating these airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks into the ALS of the existing MM or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Veteran Readiness and Employment Program: Update to Reduced Work Tolerance and Basic Eligibility Period
summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) proposes to amend the Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E) regulations to align with current practice and statute. The rule would expand the list of approved providers for reduced work tolerance (RWT) documentation, allowing for more accurate and timely processing by a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor (VRC). VA also proposes to clarify that a veteran who is subject to a basic period of eligibility would receive a new 12-year period of eligibility if such veteran obtains a compensable service-connected disability rating based on a subsequent period of active-duty service. Finally, the rule would remove the eligibility termination date for veterans discharged on or after January 1, 2013, consistent with the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020.

title: Air Plan Revisions; California; San Joaquin Valley Unified Air Pollution Control District; New Source Review; Stationary Source Permits
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is finalizing a limited approval and limited disapproval of three permitting rules as a revision to the San Joaquin Valley Unified Air Pollution Control District (SJVUAPCD or "District") portion of the California State Implementation Plan (SIP). These are revisions to the District's New Source Review (NSR) air permitting program rules for new and modified sources of air pollution under Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") section 110(a)(2)(C) and part D of title I.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3 and EC635T2+ helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that the manufacturer's service material does not provide complete instructions for the inspections after a hard landing. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection of the tail rotor control system and, depending on the inspection results, corrective actions. This proposed AD would also require revision of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-14-09, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X, FALCON 900EX, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. AD 2024-14-09 requires replacement of certain titanium screws, adds other locations for screw replacement, and revises the applicability from AD 2022-02-10. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-14-09, affected parts have been found in other areas of certain FALCON 7X airplanes as well as in additional FALCON 7X airplanes. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-14-09 and would require expanding the applicability to additional airplanes, expanding the locations for screw replacement, and revising the compliance times for parts replacement. This AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Approval and Promulgation of State Air Quality Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Texas; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or the Act), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving the CAA section 111(d) State plan submitted by the State of Texas for sources subject to the Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Landfills Emission Guidelines (EG). The Texas MSW landfills plan was submitted to fulfill the State's obligations under CAA section 111(d) to implement and enforce the requirements under the MSW Landfills EG. The EPA is approving the State plan and amending the agency regulations in accordance with the requirements of the CAA.

title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-12-17, which applies to certain ATR--GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42-300, -320, and -500 airplanes; and all Model ATR72-101, -102, -201, -202, -211, -212, and -212A airplanes. AD 2021-12-17 requires a detailed visual inspection of each affected part for deficiencies (sealant blockage and out of tolerance ligaments), and depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-12-17, it was determined that additional seat track part numbers and airplanes may be affected. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2021-12-17 and would require inspections of additional parts. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Air Plan Approval; Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) for Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) Control Technique Guidelines (CTG) Under the 2008 and 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving four State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania on May 10, 2023, January 20, 2026, February 17, 2026, and April 10, 2026, through the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (PADEP). The SIP revisions address reasonably available control technology (RACT) requirements for the 2008 and 2015 ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS) relating to control technique guidelines (CTGs) for volatile organic compounds (VOC) via previously adopted CTG regulations, three new CTG regulations and permits for four facilities covered by the CTG for the Manufacture of High-Density Polyethylene, Polypropylene, and Polystyrene Resins respectively. The EPA is approving these revisions to the Pennsylvania SIP in accordance with the requirements of the Clean Air Act (CAA).

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-15-02, which applies to all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 900 airplanes. AD 2024-15-02 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-15- 02, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-15-02 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Domestic Competitive Products Pricing and Mailing Standards Changes
summary: The Postal Service is amending Mailing Standards of the United States Postal Service, Domestic Mail Manual (DMM[supreg]), to reflect changes to prices and certain mailing standards changes scheduled for competitive products.

title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
summary: FinCEN is issuing this proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements under the Customer Due Diligence Rule consistent with the policy goals of, and as directed by, Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System. Specifically, the proposal ensures financial institutions covered by the Customer Due Diligence Rule collect sufficient information to verify the identities of beneficial owners of legal entity customers and maintain the authority, where warranted, to obtain additional information, including information relevant to whether the beneficial owners of legal entity customers possess lawful immigration status and employment authorization in the United States when such information is relevant to assessing risks.

title: Health and Human Services Acquisition Regulations; Correction
summary: This document corrects technical and typographical errors in the final rule that appeared in the Federal Register on November 18, 2015, titled "Health and Human Services Acquisition Regulations."

title: Airworthiness Directives; General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (Type Certificate Previously Held by RUAG Aerospace Services GmbH) Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (General Atomics) Model Dornier 228-100, Dornier 228-101, Dornier 228-200, Dornier 228-201, Dornier 228-202, and Dornier 228-212 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of specific part-numbered hydraulic pump motors becoming severely damaged by excessive heat. This AD requires replacing the affected hydraulic pump motor with an improved design hydraulic pump motor. This AD also prohibits installing an affected hydraulic pump motor on any airplane. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Copyright Office Fees
summary: The Copyright Office is publishing a final rule establishing adjusted fees for registration, recordation, record retrieval, search and certification, the Licensing Section services, and other services. The Office last adjusted fees in 2020, based on a study of our fiscal 2016 and 2017 costs. Since that time, the costs of providing Office services have risen substantially due to inflation and other increases. The adjusted fees are intended to enable recovery of a percentage of the Office's costs, closer to historical levels, without imposing undue barriers to access its services. This rule will take effect January 5, 2027.

title: Safety Standard for Button Cell or Coin Batteries and Consumer Products Containing Such Batteries
summary: In September 2023, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC or Commission) issued a safety standard for button cell or coin batteries and consumer products containing such products in accordance with Reese's Law. The standard incorporated by reference ANSI/UL 4200A- 2023, Standard for Safety for Products Incorporating Button Batteries or Coin Cell Batteries. UL Standards and Engagement (ULSE) has now issued a revised standard, ANSI/UL 4200A-2026. Consistent with Reese's Law, this direct final rule updates the mandatory safety standard to incorporate by reference ANSI/UL 4200A-2026.

title: Amendment of Class D and Class E Airspace; Naples, FL
summary: This action proposes to amend Class D surface airspace in Naples, FL, to properly contain instrument flight rule procedures. It also proposes to remove the Class E transition airspace extensions, as they are no longer necessary. Additionally, it proposes to reduce the Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface, as updated instrument approach procedures have lessened the need for additional airspace. Finally, it proposes administrative updates to the airspace legal description.

title: Takes of Marine Mammals Incidental to Specified Activities; Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to Military Readiness Activities in the Mariana Islands Training and Testing Study Area
summary: NMFS has received a request from the U.S. Department of the Navy (including the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Marine Corps; Navy) and on behalf of the U.S. Coast Guard (Coast Guard), U.S. Army (Army), and U.S. Air Force (Air Force) (hereafter, Navy, Coast Guard, Army, and Air Force are collectively referred to as the Action Proponents) for Incidental Take Regulations (ITR) and an associated Letter of Authorization (LOA) pursuant to the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA). The requested regulations would govern the authorization of take of marine mammals incidental to training and testing activities and modernization and sustainment of ranges conducted in the Mariana Islands Training and Testing (MITT) Study Area over the course of 7 years from July 2027 through July 2034. NMFS requests comments on this proposed rule. NMFS will consider public comments prior to making any final decision on the promulgation of the requested ITR and issuance of the LOA; agency responses to public comments will be summarized in the final rule, if issued. The Action Proponents' activities are considered military readiness activities pursuant to the MMPA, as amended by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (2004 NDAA) and the NDAA for Fiscal Year 2019 (2019 NDAA).

title: Safety Zone; Mississippi River, New Orleans, LA
summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Mississippi River near New Orleans, LA. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the response to a vessel collision and sinking. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector New Orleans, or their designated representative.

title: Reserve Requirements of Depository Institutions
summary: The Board is amending Regulation D, Reserve Requirements of Depository Institutions, to reflect the annual indexing of the reserve requirement exemption amount and the low reserve tranche for 2027. The annual indexation of these amounts is required notwithstanding the Board's action in March 2020 of setting all reserve requirement ratios to zero. The reserve requirement exemption amount for 2027 will remain $39.2 million, unchanged from 2026, consistent with the Federal Reserve Act (the "Act"). The Board is amending Regulation D to set the amount of the low reserve tranche at $688.5 million (increased from $674.1 million in 2026). The adjustment to the low reserve tranche is derived using a statutory formula specified in the Act. The annual indexation of the reserve requirement exemption amount and low reserve tranche is required by statute but will not affect depository institutions' reserve requirements, which will remain zero.

title: Proposed QPAM Re-Eligibility Options After Disqualification (QROAD) Class Prohibited Transaction Exemption
summary: This document gives notice of a proposed class prohibited transaction exemption (PTE). This proposed QROAD class PTE (Proposed QROAD Class Exemption) would allow certain qualified professional asset managers (QPAMs) to continue relying on PTE 84-14, known as the QPAM Class Exemption, even after an event that would otherwise make them ineligible under Section I(g) of that exemption. To use this alternative path, the QPAM must comply with the protective conditions in this Proposed QROAD Class Exemption, if granted. This proposal does not change any fiduciary duties under ERISA section 404 or expand the relief available under the QPAM Class Exemption.

title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Longline Retention Prohibition; Striped Marlin in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean North of the Equator
summary: NMFS is prohibiting retention of Western and Central North Pacific Ocean (WCNPO) striped marlin (Kajikia audax) by vessels registered for use under a Hawaii longline limited access permit for the remainder of 2026 because the longline fishery has reached the 2026 longline retention limit. WCNPO stiped marlin are those caught in the Pacific Ocean north of the Equator (0[deg] latitude) and west of 150[deg] W longitude. This prohibition is intended to prevent the U.S. catch limit for WCNPO striped marlin from being exceeded and ensure compliance with NMFS regulations that implement decisions of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC).

title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; General Category December Quota Transfer
summary: NMFS is adjusting the Atlantic bluefin tuna (BFT) General category December 2026 time period subquota by transferring 26 metric tons (mt) of quota from the Reserve category. This action results in a total adjusted General category December time period subquota of 42.4 mt and an adjusted Reserve category of 1 mt. This action would affect Atlantic Tunas General category (commercial) permitted vessels and Highly Migratory Species (HMS) Charter/Headboat permitted vessels with a commercial sale endorsement when fishing commercially for BFT.

title: Income Taxes
Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 SO2 NAAQS
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or Act), the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State implementation plan (SIP) revision submitted by the Commonwealth of Virginia demonstrating that Virginia satisfies the interstate transport requirements of the CAA, for the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) primary national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA proposes to find that the Virginia SIP contains adequate provisions prohibiting emissions from Commonwealth sources from contributing significantly to nonattainment or interfering with maintenance of the 2010 SO 2 NAAQS in any other State, consistent with the good neighbor provision of the CAA.

title: Air Plan Approval; Texas; Collin County Second 10-Year Maintenance Plan for the 2008 Lead Standard
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or the Act), the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a revision to the Texas State Implementation Plan (SIP) containing the State's plan for maintaining the 2008 Lead (Pb) National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS or standard) through 2037 for the Collin County area, submitted by the State of Texas, through the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) on September 25, 2025.

title: Air Plan Approval; Texas; Revisions to Concrete Batch Plant Standard Permit
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or the Act), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve revisions to the Texas State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) on April 2, 2026, to update the provisions for standard permits (SP) for concrete batch plants (CBP) that perform wet batching, dry batching, or central mixing.

title: Protecting Consumers From SIM-Swap and Port-Out Fraud
summary: In this document, the Wireline Competition Bureau (Bureau) announces that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has approved, for a period of three years, the information collection associated with Telephone Number Portability. This document is consistent with the SIM Swap and Port-Out Fraud Order, which directed the Wireline Competition Bureau to publish a document in the Federal Register announcing a compliance date of the rules.

title: Accepted Means of Compliance; Airworthiness Standards: Normal Category Airplanes
summary: This document announces the availability of ASTM International (ASTM) consensus standards for use as an FAA-accepted means of compliance (MOC) to the applicable airworthiness standards for normal category airplanes. The FAA accepts ASTM F3264-25, "Standard Specification for Normal Category Aeroplanes Certification," with changes identified in this document.

title: Automatic Enrollment Requirements Under Section 414A
summary: This document sets forth final regulations that provide guidance with respect to the automatic enrollment requirements that apply to certain retirement plans. The regulations reflect statutory changes made by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 requiring that certain cash or deferred arrangements and salary reduction agreements be eligible automatic contribution arrangements that satisfy additional specified requirements. The regulations affect participants in, beneficiaries of, employers maintaining, and administrators of certain retirement plans that include cash or deferred arrangements or annuity contracts purchased under salary reduction agreements and other retirement plans that include eligible automatic contribution arrangements.

title: Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools; Hearing
summary: This document provides a notice of an additional date for the public hearing on the notice of proposed rulemaking (REG-119986-25) published in the Federal Register on Friday, September 4, 2026. The proposed regulations would provide that a private school is not described as an organization exempt from Federal income tax if it discriminates on the basis of race, color, or national or ethnic origin in administration of its educational, admissions, scholarship, athletic, or other policies, based on the fundamental public policy of the United States against such practices.
